why: A June 2025 preprint claims a proof that quasiperfect numbers do not exist, and separate 2025-2026 arXiv papers report improved bounds on the problem's own quantities (minimum size raised toward 10^45, minimum distinct prime factors raised from seven to eight).

found.title: A Note on Quasiperfect Numbers
found.note: Preprint claiming a proof by contradiction that no quasiperfect number exists; not read, not peer reviewed.

found.title: Computing bounded solutions to linear Diophantine equations with the sum of divisors
found.note: Reported to raise the lower bound on a hypothetical quasiperfect number from 10^35 to 10^45; not read.

found.title: Every quasiperfect number has at least eight distinct prime factors
found.note: Reported to improve the minimum distinct prime factor count from seven (standing since 1982) to eight; not read.
